claims.statement: Berhanu et al. power a cell-free protein synthesis system with ATP made by light in proteoliposomes and program it with a GFP gene. Protein appears only in the complete reaction: leaving out the T7 RNA polymerase, the DNA, the proteoliposomes or the light each gives no detectable GFP, and inside giant vesicles the transcription-translation reaction produces fluorescent protein in about 15 percent of the vesicles. claims.statement: Hibi et al. run a reconstituted translation system with no native tRNA and supply instead 21 unmodified tRNAs made by transcription, which support synthesis of full-length DHFR and sfGFP whose yield rises with the amount of tRNA added. They then move the CGA anticodon into tRNA-Ala, whose synthetase recognizes the acceptor stem and not the anticodon, drop the original alanine tRNA, and rewrite every alanine codon of a DHFR gene as the serine codon UCG. The same gene then yields two different proteins: with the redesigned tRNA set UCG is read as alanine, confirmed by mass spectrometry, and the DHFR is active, whereas with native tRNAs, which read UCG as serine, the DHFR made is inactive. studies.finding: Mixing the folded multivalent proteins produced sharp liquid-liquid demixing: SH34 with PRM4 at 300 microM modules gave spherical droplets of about 1 to more than 50 micrometres that coalesced over time and concentrated both proteins about 100-fold (116-fold for SH35+PRM5). The phase boundary depended strongly on valency, and phase separation was blocked by the monovalent ligand PRM(H)1 and absent with PRM1, which cannot polymerise, while PRM2 and PRM4 increased the apparent radii before droplet formation. Electron-dense objects of 50-500 nm appeared only in the mixtures, not with either protein alone or below the droplet concentration, and in cells puncta formed only on co-expression of the two high-valency proteins. In the nephrin/Nck/N-WASP system droplet formation shifted the phase boundary with the degree of nephrin phosphorylation, and actin assembly by the Arp2/3 complex rose sharply as the total N-WASP concentration crossed the droplet boundary. The authors conclude that interactions between multivalent macromolecules produce sharp liquid-liquid phase separation coupled to a sol-gel transition.
limitations: The SH3 and PRM constructs are engineered repeat proteins, and the nephrin system is reconstituted in vitro, so the concentrations and geometry need not match a cell.

The folded SH3 domain is not unfolded in a control, so the experiment shows condensates forming from multivalent folded domains rather than that folding is required for phase separation; condensates of disordered proteins are known from other work.

The sol-gel transition inside the droplets is inferred from scattering, photobleaching and cryo-EM edges, not observed directly, and the supplementary simulations and cyclization analysis were not read.
The actin assembly readout is a half-time in a bulk pyrene assay, and the sharp rise is correlated with the separately determined phase boundary rather than measured in the same reaction.
studies.observable: Presence and size of liquid droplets and the phase boundary in module concentration; partition coefficients; hydrodynamic and gyration radii; fluorescence recovery; half-time of Arp2/3-mediated actin assembly
studies.preparation: Mix purified multivalent proteins at defined module concentrations in aqueous buffer and score droplet formation by bright-field and fluorescence microscopy after more than 12 hours; map phase boundaries against valency. Test whether assembly drives demixing by adding a high-affinity monovalent ligand PRM(H)1, and follow species size by dynamic light scattering and small-angle X-ray scattering during PRM titrations into SH35, with droplets removed by centrifugation. Image droplets by electron cryo-microscopy and measure exchange by photobleaching. In cells, co-express mCherry-SH35 with eGFP-PRM5 or eGFP-PRM3. For function, measure pyrene-actin assembly with fixed Arp2/3 complex, Nck, triply phosphorylated nephrin peptide and N-WASP plus increasing amounts of an N-WASP truncation that polymerises but cannot bind Arp2/3. Controls: single components alone, low-valency partners, mixtures below the droplet concentration and an N-WASP lacking the proline-rich region.
